stem.text: Water flows into a tank at the rate \( R(t) = 5 \sin{\left(\frac{t^{2}}{2} \right)} + 9 \) gallons per hour, where t is measured in hours for \( 0 \le t \le 5 \). The tank holds 90 gallons of water at time \( t = 0 \). During the same time, water flows out through a drain at the rate \( D(t) = t + \frac{9}{2} \) gallons per hour. Using a calculator, find the total number of gallons that arrive during the time interval \( 1 \le t \le 4 \). Show the setup, and give the value correct to three decimal places.

worked_solution.text: The amount that arrives is the integral of the inflow rate over the interval, \( \int_{1}^{4} \left(5 \sin{\left(\frac{t^{2}}{2} \right)} + 9\right)\,dt \), and nothing is added for the starting amount or taken away.
With the calculator in radian mode, the integral is about 30.719 gallons.

options.derivation: the integral evaluated with the calculator in degree mode
the amount present at the end reported, the starting amount added to the integral of the inflow
the rate evaluated at the endpoints and subtracted, R(b) - R(a), in place of its integral
